english.title: Employer fail to keep records to establish remuneration of employees was at least equal to national minimum wage
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the employer of a worker, namely **(..SPECIFY WORKER..), who qualified for the national minimum wage, failed to keep in respect of that worker, for a period of three years beginning with the day upon which the pay reference period immediately following that to which they related ends, records sufficient to establish that you were remunerating

(A)_[him,]_
(B)_[her,]_

at a rate at least equal to the national minimum wage in a form which enabled the information kept about that worker in respect of a pay reference period to be produced in a single document
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 59(1), (2) and (8) of the National Minimum Wage Regulations 2015 and section 31(2) and (9) of the National Minimum Wage Act 1998.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
employer of a worker who qualified for the national minimum wage
failed to keep records
for period specified in reg 59(8)
sufficient to establish worker was remunerated
at rate at least equal to the NMW
in form which enabled relevant information to be produced in single document

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: A fine

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
